summary: Humboldt County lookout on BLM land above Kneeland: a CCC-era L-701 design with a later cab, abandoned by CAL FIRE and still standing despite a 2011 demolition notice.

facts.design: single-story variation of the CCC-era Forest Service L-701 tower, with a 732-6A cab
facts.status_note: Abandoned by CAL FIRE. A 2011 notice planned demolition, but it still stood in May 2019 and was described as standing in 2023.

access.note: The approach runs over private roads with locked gates and private-property signs. The lookout stands on BLM land that a 2023 hiker says has no right of way. The sources read give no sign of public access.

visit.trail_note: A 2023 hike parked on Kneeland Road and walked up unsigned Slater Road. A locked gate below the lookout and private-property signs blocked the final approach.

facts.agency: CAL FIRE Humboldt-Del Norte Unit; site on BLM Arcata Field Office land under a lease from BLM

events.note: Rangers judged a fire lookout station necessary at Iaqua Buttes; a telephone line was needed so outside aid could be called in during a fire emergency. Newspaper report, December 28, 1928.
Register gives 1936 as the build date (Built field 1936/1976). A 1938 newspaper describes construction of a steel lookout; the sources do not say whether these are the same tower.
Mrs. Francis Slater in charge of the lookout's telephone (Blue Lake Advocate, May 30, 1936, as transcribed).
Newspaper (Ukiah Daily Journal, June 18, 1938, as transcribed) reports construction of a steel lookout at Iaqua Buttes, reached only by pack train. Conflicts with the Register's 1936 date.
Year of the Hugh Slater notice (Eureka Humboldt Times, October 17, 1957). The couple worked there as lookout attendants for 20 years; the period is not dated.
Second date in the Register's Built field. The page does not say what changed.
CAL FIRE notice of exemption, received May 31, 2011, describes formal closure, lease termination and demolition. The sources read do not confirm the demolition was carried out.
Register: 'still stands as of a May 2019 Trip Report'.
Date registered per the Register: October 19, 2019.
Hiker's February 2023 post calls the structure abandoned by CAL FIRE and says it stands at the top of the Buttes.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 2011 CAL FIRE notice planned demolition, and the Register says the lookout was slated for removal until 2012. It still stood in May 2019 and was described as standing in 2023. The sources read do not show that the demolition was carried out.

sources.title: Iaqua Buttes Fire Lookout Station - Facilities Demolition

notes_for_editor: Register number conflict: the NHLR detail page gives US 1317, CA 140, which matches the record. The FFLA California list gives US 1387, CA 210. Built date: the Register says 1936 (Built field 1936/1976); a 1938 newspaper describes a steel lookout's construction. The sources do not say whether these are one tower; left open in the story. Storey count: the Register says single-story, the 2023 hiker says two-story. Demolition: the 2011 notice planned it; the 2019 and 2023 sources say it stands; no source shows the demolition. The blog's statement that the lookout was built shortly after 1928 is unsourced and not used. Ownership is 'unknown' in the record; the 2011 notice places the site on BLM land under a lease, so the editor may want to set it. Access: locked gates and private roads per the 2023 hike; check with BLM Arcata Field Office before any change to the access note.
